text:
mike: Heads up — autotuner run on mi250 farm found a gap: several int8 tiling primitives not registered for new conv kernel variant.
ciara: ugh. which primitives?
raj: looks like `mi250_int8_tiling_v2` and `mi250_int8_conv_fastpath` are missing from the dispatch table. get_kernel() returns NotFound during model load.
sarah: seen a few OOMs during warmup, maybe because fallback switched to generic fp16 path? any logs?
mike: pasted the loader error from a failing job:
```
[loader] WARNING: kernel_lookup: mi250_int8_tiling_v2 not found for op aten::conv1d seq=512 batch=8
[loader] ERROR: fallback to generic_gemm_fp16 (perf delta +18%)
```
ciara: perf delta +18% is rough. was this on a seq=512 eval or production load test?
raj: seq=512 eval harness. interestingly autotuner marked the primitive as 'incompatible_signature' not 'missing', so it removed it from candidates during compile.
sarah: so runtime sees it as unavailable even though the binary exists on disk?
raj: yeah — the signature mismatch happens when padding/strides heuristics produce a nonstandard layout. the kernel metadata expects row-major contiguous input; autotuner output sometimes registers with layout=packed. mismatch => not eligible.
mike: proposal: add a soft-route that will attempt a relaxed-signature match at runtime and mark such kernels as "soft-available" so conditional routing can try them if the SLO allows. fallback policy: prefer soft-available over generic_gemm_fp16 when latency headroom > 15ms.
ciara: could we also teach the autotuner to emit a shim that reorders strides when safe? cheaper than relaxed-matching?
raj: maybe, but shim adds copy cost — need microbenchmarks. I ran a quick batch-profile showing shim copy cost ~2-3ms for small batches, but for batch>=16 copy amortizes.
perf-bot: Profile snapshot: https://perf.internal/runs/212345/summary — shows 12% tail latency bump when falling back to generic_gemm_fp16 vs soft-route candidates.
sarah: another variable: KV-cache hit rate. when cache hits are high, sequences are shorter and we often hit the int8 fastpath prerequisites (no padding). low KV hit rates produce edge-case layouts that trip the signature mismatch.
mike: long-term: we should (1) update autotuner to emit both strict and relaxed registrations, (2) add a runtime relaxed-dispatch pass with safety checks, (3) add sequence-length aware routing that biases toward conservative kernels for low-KV-hit workloads.
ciara: agree. short-term mitigation? add a compatibility shim in the kernel registry that maps `mi250_int8_tiling_v2_variantA` -> `mi250_int8_tiling_v2` when stride/layout differ only by a known permutation. quick patch should reduce immediate regressions.
raj: I'll open an RFC+PR with a registry shim and an opt-in relaxed-dispatch flag. we can flip flag on a subset of Dedicated capacity for canary.
sarah: please add an eval run that compares token-per-second and tail P99 across KV hit buckets (0-25%, 25-75%, 75-100%). want numbers before enabling relaxed dispatch widely.
mike: noted. I'll own the eval and the canary rollout plan. thanks all :thumbsup:
